scenarios.title: Sudden crash
scenarios.expectation: Equities fall 9% in a day and their intervals double: the LLM reduces risk (invested share at least 2 points below the baseline).

runs.detail: invested 85.1% against 90.0% at the baseline
runs.analysis: Final decision after tool exploration (5 of 12 calls used). Timestral 5-day forecasts show a high-volatility regime following a broad 20-day selloff (SPY -17.4%, QQQ -21.4%, EEM -21.0%, NVDA -45.9% over 20d), with the portfolio -4% from peak under an active 'alert' drawdown action. The current book equals the baseline, is guardrail-accepted, and has no dominant risk share (top-5 all ~8.5-10%), so no position is structurally mis-sized. The concrete triggers for a modest defensive change are: (1) the drawdown alert, (2) elevated forecast interval widths/volatility in QQQ (width_80 0.325, vol 12.7%), EEM (0.308, 12.0%), AMZN (0.299, 11.6%), and (3) NVDA's extreme outlier risk (width_80 0.70, q05 -47.3%, vol 27.4%). Evaluated candidate vs current portfolio: trimming QQQ/EEM/AMZN by 1pt each and zeroing NVDA, lifting cash from 10% to 14.89%, trades only 4.9 points, cuts forecast volatility from 3.23% to 2.74% (-15%) and improves the 5% bad case from -11.63% to -11.42%; guardrails report 'accepted' with no breaches. A deeper 20% cash variant traded 10.4 points for only marginal additional risk reduction and was rejected as churn. TLT (24.4%, vol 1.6%, only asset with positive 5d return +2.6%) stays as ballast near its 25% cap. All constraints verified: long-only, weights sum to 1.0, cash 14.89% >= 10%, every ETF <= 25%, every stock <= 10%, every group <= 30% (tech_growth 3.8%, financials 11.6%, health 11.7%, energy 10.0%, us_broad 8.5%), points traded 4.9 < 30, drawdown action is 'alert' only (no reduce_only/cap_exposure_60).

runs.detail: invested 80.5% against 90.0% at the baseline
runs.analysis: Final decision. Tools (5d forecasts, last close 2026-11-20) show interval width and volatility as the reliable risk signal: NVDA width 0.70/vol 27.4%, QQQ 0.325/12.7%, EEM 0.308/12.0%, AMZN 0.299/11.6%, SPY 0.250/9.8%, versus TLT 0.040/1.6%, XLV 0.142, XLF 0.141, GLD 0.119. Medians have no directional skill, so they are not used as signals. The portfolio is in a -4% drawdown with 'alert', and every equity is down hard over 20d (-10% to -46%; only TLT is positive at +0.6%). Current portfolio 5d forecast: q05 -11.63%, vol 3.23%, balanced risk shares (SPY 10.0%, EFA 9.7%, IWM 9.5%, QQQ 8.9%, EEM 8.5%). Concrete trigger for change: the drawdown alert plus the three widest equity intervals (QQQ, EEM, AMZN) in a falling market. I evaluated trimming exactly those three to zero (9.5 points traded, cash 10% -> 19.47%): q05 improves to -10.79% (+0.84 pts), forecast vol falls to 2.54% (-0.69 pts, -21%), guardrails report 'accepted', and all caps hold (TLT 24.44% <= 25%, each stock <= 10%, every group <= 30%, cash >= 10%, 9.5 pts traded <= 30%). A partial trim was tested and was strictly worse on both q05 and vol, so the full trim of those three names is the change. NVDA's interval is the widest but its 1.39% weight cannot be reduced by a tradable >=2 points and it is not a top-5 risk share, so it stays. All other positions are held: no material trigger, and churn is avoided.

runs.detail: invested 88.6% against 90.0% at the baseline
runs.analysis: Tools used: 5-day and 1-day Timestral forecasts for all 15 assets, the inverse-width baseline, and portfolio evaluations of the current book plus two candidates. The current portfolio equals the baseline, is guardrail-accepted, has balanced risk shares (SPY/EFA/IWM/QQQ/EEM each ~8-10%, top-5 ~46%), forecast vol 3.23%, q05 -11.6%. Drawdown is -4% with only an 'alert' action, so no reduce-only or exposure cap applies. The one material signal is NVDA: 5-day interval width 0.70 (q05 -47.3%, vol 27.4%), more than twice the next-widest asset (QQQ 0.32), after a -45.9% 20-day and -29.9% 5-day move. Trimming NVDA from 1.39% to 0 into cash trades only 1.43 points and cuts forecast volatility by 0.22pp (3.23%->3.01%) with the bad case q05 essentially unchanged (-0.03pp); the alternative (0.5% NVDA stub + TLT to the 25% cap) traded more points for a smaller vol cut (-0.14pp) and added duration concentration, so it was rejected. All other positions stay at current weights: no other interval widened or narrowed materially, risk shares are balanced, and medians carry no directional skill, so no other change has a concrete trigger. Cash rises to 11.39% (above the 10% floor).

scenarios.title: One very uncertain asset
scenarios.expectation: NVDA's forecast interval is four times wider: the LLM does not pile into it.

runs.detail: NVDA -0.0 pts against its (already small) baseline
runs.analysis: Final decision after tool exploration at the 5-day horizon. The current portfolio equals the inverse-interval-width baseline (90% invested / 10% cash, no drawdown, guardrails accept it as-is) and forecasts q05 = -6.49%, vol 1.74%, with risk well spread (top-5 risk shares 9-11%, nothing dominant). The one concrete, nameable trigger is the concentration of forecast uncertainty in the growth sleeve: QQQ (width_80 0.162, vol 6.3%), EEM (0.154, 6.0%) and AMZN (0.149, 5.8%) carry the widest intervals and highest vols in the book after NVDA (width 1.41, but only 0.43% weight, below the 2-point trade threshold), and all suffered the deepest recent drawdowns (QQQ -13.6% and EEM -13.2% over 20d). TLT is the mirror image: narrowest interval (0.040), lowest vol (1.6%), and the only asset with positive 1d/5d/20d returns. I evaluated a defensive tilt with evaluate_portfolio: trimming QQQ/EEM/AMZN by 2 points each into TLT (+4) and cash (+2) trades 10.03 points (well inside the 30-point limit), cuts forecast vol by 0.19pp to 1.55% and improves the bad case q05 by +0.78pp to -5.71%, with risk shares still balanced (max 11.7%); a milder 6-point variant bought only +0.51pp of q05 improvement, so the 10-point move is the better trade. Guardrails accept the allocation: cash 12% (>=10%), TLT 19.14% (<25% ETF cap), largest stock 8.61% (<10%), group totals tech_growth 4.2%, financials 14.4%, energy 12.4%, health 14.5% (all <30%). Median forecasts show no directional skill, so the decision rests on interval width/vol and the bad case, which is exactly what this change improves. All other positions are kept at current weights — no drawdown, no cap breach, no dominant risk share justifies further churn.

runs.detail: largest increase -0.0 pts (reduce-only is active)

My evaluated candidate cuts QQQ, EEM, AMZN roughly in half and trims GLD, raising cash from 10% to 18.3%: versus the current portfolio it trades 8.3 points (well under the 30% cap), cuts forecast volatility to 1.46% (-0.26 pts) and improves the 5-day bad case q05 to -5.97% (+0.76 pts). Guardrails accept it; cash >= 10%, all ETF/stock/group caps satisfied (tech_growth 5.3%, financials 14.1%, energy 12.2%, health 14.3%), reduce_only respected (every changed weight is below current; held weights set a hair below current to pass the drawdown float check). NVDA is kept despite the highest vol (13.7%) because at 1.7% weight its risk share is small and a further trim would be below the 2-point trading threshold.
